1	# Comparator verification of the headline theorems
     2	
     3	Two challenges are configured, one per headline result: the LDT challenge
     4	for `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` and the QPBT challenge for
     5	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` and `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit`.
     6	They share the generation tooling in `scripts/comparator/`, the drift guard
     7	and the trust model below; each lives in its own challenge repository.
     8	
     9	## The LDT challenge
    10	
    11	The headline theorem `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` (the corrected source
    12	statement of `thm:main-formal` from the low individual degree test paper) is
    13	independently verifiable with the official
    14	[leanprover/comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator), the
    15	top level of the escalating checks in the Lean reference manual's
    16	[Validating Proofs](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/ValidatingProofs/)
    17	chapter.
    18	
    19	Following community practice
    20	([lamplighter-comparator](https://github.com/vidick/lamplighter-comparator),
    21	[erdos-unit-distance-comparator](https://github.com/kim-em/erdos-unit-distance-comparator)),
    22	the challenge lives in a separate repository —
    23	**[LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator)** —
    24	which requires this library as a lake dependency pinned by commit:
    25	
    26	- `Challenge.lean` there imports **only Mathlib** and re-declares, verbatim
    27	  and in dependency order, every declaration in the comparator-relevant
    28	  closure of the statement of `mainFormal` (111 declarations, ~1200 lines),
    29	  then states the theorem with `sorry`.  It is the entire human audit
    30	  surface.
    31	- `Solution.lean` there imports this library, which proves the theorem under
    32	  the same fully-qualified names; no bridging lemmas are needed.
    33	- Its CI runs the comparator (real landrun sandbox, nanoda external kernel,
    34	  `lean4checker` re-check) on every push and weekly.
    35	
    36	## What this repository contributes
    37	
    38	1. **Environment alignment.**  Comparator compares, constant by constant, the
    39	   full kernel closure of the statement — types, definition bodies, and the
    40	   proofs embedded in them — so `Challenge.lean` must elaborate to
    41	   bit-identical terms.  Every module contributing a declaration to the
    42	   closure therefore uses the full `import Mathlib` (directly or through
    43	   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean` /
    44	   `MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`), so tactic elaboration sees
    45	   the same environment as the Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  The four
    46	   modules with direct Mathlib imports carry a comment saying not to narrow
    47	   them.  (Measured impact: only 14 modules that did not already see full
    48	   Mathlib through `Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean` gained it.)
    49	2. **Regeneration tooling.**  `scripts/comparator/` holds the closure
    50	   extractor (a Lean metaprogram mirroring comparator's `runForUsedConsts`)
    51	   and the assembler that produce `Challenge.lean`.  After changing any
    52	   definition in the closure: regenerate per `scripts/comparator/README.md`,
    53	   copy the result into LDT-comparator, and bump its library pin.
    54	
    55	## Checklist against the official *Validating Proofs* guide
    56	
    57	| Level | Requirement | Status |
    58	|---|---|---|
    59	| 2 | `#print axioms` shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean`; also enforced by comparator's `permitted_axioms` |
    60	| 3 | `lean4checker --fresh` re-check | `lean4checker: true` in the comparator repo's lean-action step |
    61	| 4 | Statement written in a trusted environment, separate from proof code | `Challenge.lean` imports only Mathlib (CI-enforced grep); separate repo, library pinned by commit |
    62	| 4 | Sandboxed build + export + kernel replay | official comparator binary (pinned to the toolchain tag), real landrun in CI |
    63	| 4 | External checker in addition to the Lean kernel | `enable_nanoda = true` (pinned nanoda tag); local macOS runs use `./verify.sh --fake-landrun` which disables it |
    64	| 5 | No native evaluation (`Lean.trustCompiler`, `decide +native`) | excluded by `permitted_axioms` — comparator rejects any extra axiom |
    65	| — | Statement review: custom notation and type classes must not obscure meaning | `Challenge.lean` uses no custom notation; review of it is the human step |
    66	
    67	Deliberate deviations from the comparator README's adversarial setup, per its
    68	own guidance for trusted trees: the `systemd-run` landrun-escape guard is
    69	omitted and prebuilt `.lake` artifacts are reused, because both modules come
    70	from a trusted checkout rather than an untrusted submitter.
    71	
    72	Residual trust: Lean's logical soundness, comparator's own plumbing, sandbox
    73	security, simultaneous bugs in all checkers, and human error in
    74	`Challenge.lean` itself — keep that file short, notation-free, and reviewed.
    75	
    76	## The QPBT challenge
    77	
    78	The QPBT headline theorems `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` (`thm:pauli`) and
    79	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` (`cor:pauli-binary`) get the same
    80	treatment, in the separate repository
    81	**[QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator)**.
    82	
    83	- **Targets.**  Both theorems are verified in one comparator run
    84	  (`theorem_names` lists both), so the challenge re-declares the union of the
    85	  two statement closures.
    86	- **Closure size.**  190 declarations from twenty library
    87	  modules, about 2700 lines — larger than the LDT challenge because the
    88	  Pauli basis test carries the full question/answer combinatorics
    89	  (`PauliType`, `PauliAnswer`, the win predicate and the question
    90	  distribution) into the statement.
    91	- **Generated file.**  `scripts/comparator/expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected`,
    92	  regenerated and byte-compared by the same drift guard as the LDT challenge
    93	  (`--challenge qpbt`).
    94	
    95	### Environment alignment for QPBT
    96	
    97	Comparator compares the full kernel closure constant by constant, so the
    98	Mathlib-only challenge file must elaborate to bit-identical terms.  Two
    99	obstacles had to be removed in the library:
   100	
   101	1. **Narrowed imports.**  Four closure modules —
   102	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Subspaces.lean`,
   103	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Coefficients.lean`,
   104	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/LowDegreeCode.lean` and
   105	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Lines.lean` — imported individual Mathlib files, so
   106	   tactic elaboration there saw a smaller environment than the challenge file
   107	   would.  They now use the full `import Mathlib` and carry the same "do not
   108	   narrow this import" comment as the LDT base modules.  The remaining sixteen
   109	   closure modules already saw full Mathlib through
   110	   `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean` or
   111	   `MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`.
   112	2. **Private closure members.**  A `private` declaration's real name is
   113	   qualified by its defining module (`_private.<module>.0.<name>`), so a
   114	   challenge file in a different module can never re-declare it under the
   115	   library's name.  Nineteen closure members were private — twelve in
   116	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/FieldBasis.lean` (the self-dual normal basis
   117	   construction that `fixedFieldModel` selects from), six in
   118	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Subspaces.lean` (the pivot-rank machinery behind
   119	   `canonicalComplement`), and `singlePauliVec` in
   120	   `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/Pauli.lean`.  Dropping `private` is the smallest
   121	   faithful edit: no statement, definition body or proof script changes, only
   122	   the visibility of names that the statement closure already depends on.
   123	
   124	No statement of either headline theorem changed, and their axiom closure
   125	remains `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.
   126	
   127	The "do not narrow this import" notes on the shared base modules
   128	(`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/ParametersBase.lean`,
   129	`MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`,
   130	`MIPStarRE/Quantum/FiniteMatrix/Basic.lean`) still name only `mainFormal`,
   131	and deliberately so: those modules contribute to both closures, and adding a
   132	line to a module docstring shifts every declaration below it, which would
   133	rewrite the `-- source:` provenance comments of the checked-in LDT challenge.
   134	They are covered by this section instead.
   135	
   136	### Regenerating and auditing
   137	
   138	Regeneration is the pipeline in `scripts/comparator/README.md` with
   139	`--challenge qpbt`.  After an intentional change to any definition in the
   140	closure: regenerate, copy the expected file into QPBT-comparator as
   141	`Challenge.lean`, bump the `rev` pin in its `lakefile.toml` to the library
   142	commit it was generated from, and run its `./verify.sh`.
   143	
   144	What the human must audit, and what no tool can check: that
   145	`ChallengeQPBT.lean` really states the intended theorems.  Concretely, that
   146	the Pauli basis test it defines — `pauliQuestionDistribution`,
   147	`pauliWinPredicate`, `pauliBasisTest` — is the test of the paper; that
   148	`deltaQld` is the paper's error functional; that `PauliSoundnessWitness` and
   149	`QubitSoundnessWitness` package isometries and an auxiliary state without
   150	smuggling in a hypothesis; and that `Strategy.value` and the operator
   151	distances mean what their names claim.  Everything else in the file is
   152	machine-checked to agree with the library.
   153	
   154	## Benchmark use
   155	
   156	The same statement is submission-ready for
   157	[leanprover/lean-eval](https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval) (the official
   158	comparator-based benchmark behind [lean-lang.org/eval](https://lean-lang.org/eval/)):
   159	port the statement module to lean-eval's toolchain, tag the theorem
   160	`@[eval_problem]`, add a `manifests/problems/<id>.toml` (`holes`, `submitter`,
   161	`source`, `informal_solution`), and open a PR to lean-eval.  Large
   162	self-contained statement preludes have precedent there (the knot-theory
   163	problems ship a 23 KB trusted `ChallengeDeps.lean`).  Solvers edit only
   164	`Submission.lean`; scoring is comparator acceptance, with submissions run by
   165	the Lean FRO's hosted pipeline.
     1	# The ITP artifact
     2	
     3	This page is for two audiences: a **reviewer** who received the artifact
     4	tarball and wants to check that the claimed theorems really are proved, and a
     5	**maintainer** who has to cut the next snapshot.
     6	
     7	The artifact is a **release snapshot of the mathematical development**, not the
     8	working repository. It is produced by `scripts/make_artifact.sh` from a tagged
     9	commit, and every copy carries a `MANIFEST.txt` naming the commit it came from.
    10	
    11	## What is in it
    12	
    13	| path | what it is |
    14	|---|---|
    15	| `MIPStarRE/`, `MIPStarRE.lean` | the Lean 4 development — the contribution |
    16	| `lakefile.toml`, `lake-manifest.json`, `lean-toolchain` | the pinned build: Lean 4 and all ten dependencies by exact revision |
    17	| `blueprint/src/` | the LaTeX blueprint, cross-referenced to the Lean names with `\lean{}` / `\leanok` |
    18	| `docs/` | the mathematical documentation, including `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md` (every headline and supporting statement with its Lean name, blueprint label and paper locator) and `docs/paper-gaps/` (the register of gaps found in the source papers) |
    19	| `references/` | the TeX sources of the five source papers — third-party material, see below — so that the paper locators can be checked inside the snapshot; the report below records two existing exceptions |
    20	| `scripts/comparator/` | the generator for the self-contained `Challenge.lean` statement file used by the independent challenge repository |
    21	| `scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py` | the blueprint/axiom consistency check |
    22	| `scripts/make_artifact.sh` | the script that produced this snapshot, so the packaging is itself auditable |
    23	| `MANIFEST.txt` | source commit, file count, Lean code-line total, toolchain, Mathlib revision, leak-scan and self-containment results |
    24	
    25	## What is **not** in it, and why
    26	
    27	**The AI-workflow layer.** This development was produced with a local
    28	agent-orchestration layer: `local/`, `results/telemetry/`, `.github/` prompts
    29	and workflows, `.githooks/`, `audits/`, `home_page/`, `docbuild/`, and the
    30	scripts and docs that only serve that layer. It stays in the source repository
    31	because it is research material in its own right, but it is not part of the
    32	mathematics and it dominates the repository's size (the telemetry session logs
    33	alone are roughly 200 MB). Excluding it also removes, without any history
    34	rewrite, the ~2,456 tracked files that mention the build host's home path.
    35	
    36	## Third-party material: the paper sources, `references/`
    37	
    38	The snapshot ships the TeX sources of the five papers the development is
    39	formalized from (owner decision, 2026-09-19, following the companion
    40	low-degree-test repository, which likewise keeps its paper sources in the
    41	public repository):
    42	
    43	| path | paper | arXiv |
    44	|---|---|---|
    45	| `references/qpbt-paper/` | *MIP\* = RE* (primary source) | arXiv:2001.04383 |
    46	| `references/neexp-paper/` | *NEEXP in MIP\** (secondary source) | arXiv:1904.05870 |
    47	| `references/ldt-paper/` | low individual degree test | arXiv:2009.12982 |
    48	| `references/nv-paper/` | Natarajan–Vidick | arXiv:1610.03574 |
    49	| `references/cs-paper/` | see `references/cs-paper/SOURCE.md` | — |
    50	
    51	**Why they ship.** Lean docstrings and `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md` cite their
    52	source as `references/<paper>/<file>.tex:<lines>`, and so will
    53	`docs/DEVIATIONS.md` when it lands (it is pending in another packet, and the
    54	two `README.md` links to it are the two dead internal-link occurrences that
    55	`MANIFEST.txt` still reports). With the sources in the snapshot all but the two
    56	locators listed below resolve inside the tarball, and a reviewer can read the
    57	paper statement next to the Lean statement without reconstructing the
    58	per-section split from arXiv. The directories are plain per-section splits of
    59	the papers' arXiv sources.
    60	
    61	**Licence.** These files are the work of their own authors and are **not**
    62	covered by the Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` that ships with the snapshot and governs the
    63	development itself. They are kept here for reference and for line-precise
    64	citation; their own terms govern any further use or redistribution. The
    65	`MANIFEST.txt` of every snapshot repeats this.
    66	
    67	**Locator report.** `MANIFEST.txt` records how many of the
    68	`references/<paper>/<file>.tex` paths cited in the Lean sources, the blueprint
    69	and the docs actually resolve inside the snapshot. It is a report, not a gate:
    70	a locator may name a section the per-file split arranges differently. The
    71	gap-note template's fill-in placeholder is not counted (the mirrors' file names
    72	are lower case, so a locator with a capital in it is a form to complete rather
    73	than a citation). At the commit named in the MANIFEST two do not resolve —
    74	`references/ldt-paper/commutativity_points.tex` and
    75	`references/ldt-paper/projectivization.tex`, cited from
    76	`MIPStarRE/LDT/CommutativityPoints/AnswerTheorems.lean` and
    77	`MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/Orthonormalization.lean`. They
    78	predate this packaging work and are tracked separately; the surrounding
    79	docstrings also name their blueprint labels, which do resolve.
    80	
    81	**Leak scan.** The scan that gates packaging (below) treats these files like
    82	any other: a home path or a key-shaped string inside `references/` still fails
    83	the run. The one forgiveness is scoped to `references/` by path and to
    84	e-mail addresses by content — the corresponding-author addresses printed in the
    85	papers' own front matter, which are third-party material reproduced as
    86	published, not contact addresses of this development. It is recorded as a
    87	`LEAK_ALLOW_IN` entry in `scripts/make_artifact.sh` with that reason, and a
    88	blanket entry was deliberately not used: the scan must still catch an address of
    89	ours anywhere else in the snapshot.
    90	
    91	## Verifying the artifact as a reviewer
    92	
    93	### 1. Install the pinned toolchain
    94	
    95	```sh
    96	curl https://elan.lean-lang.org/elan-init.sh -sSf | sh   # if elan is not installed
    97	cd <unpacked snapshot>
    98	cat lean-toolchain     # leanprover/lean4:v4.32.0 — elan installs this on first use
    99	```
   100	
   101	### 2. Fetch the Mathlib build cache and build
   102	
   103	```sh
   104	lake exe cache get
   105	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Expected cost.** `lake exe cache get` downloads several GB. Plan on **16 GB
   109	of RAM** and tens of GB of disk. At this source commit, these commands count
   110	occurrences and files, respectively:
   111	
   112	```sh
   113	rg -n -o 'maxHeartbeats' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   114	rg -l 'maxHeartbeats' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   115	rg -n -o 'synthInstance\.maxSize' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   116	rg -l 'synthInstance\.maxSize' MIPStarRE | wc -l
   117	```
   118	
   119	They report 38 occurrences across 23 files for `maxHeartbeats`, and 66 across
   120	17 files for `synthInstance.maxSize`, so this is not a laptop build. Honest
   121	statement of the evidence we have: the maintainers' build telemetry records
   122	1,608 builds of this development, but every one is an
   123	*incremental, warm-cache* build (the two most recent took 79 s and 556 s); the
   124	only full-rebuild record, 25,052 s (7 h), is from 2026-08-30 and predates most
   125	of the QPBT development. **A cold clean-clone build of `MIPStarRE.QPBT` has not
   126	yet been recorded**; when one is, its wall-clock time and machine replace this
   127	paragraph. Budget several hours.
   128	
   129	### 3. Check that nothing is assumed
   130	
   131	The development claims to depend on no axioms beyond Lean's three standard
   132	ones — `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` — and on no `sorry`,
   133	`admit`, `native_decide`, `unsafe` or `@[extern]` escape hatch.
   134	
   135	The check that settles the first half is Lean's own `#print axioms`: it reports
   136	the complete axiom closure of a declaration, and unlike a text search it cannot
   137	be misled by prose. The snapshot ships two modules that run it at build time and
   138	**fail the build** when a declaration's closure is not exactly
   139	`{Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext}` — one for the Pauli test, one for the
   140	classical low-individual-degree layer underneath it:
   141	
   142	```sh
   143	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit
   144	lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit
   145	```
   146	
   147	`MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.AxiomAudit` covers the four headline theorems of section 4
   148	and nine further load-bearing statements; the printed axiom lines stay in the
   149	build log as the positive record. Neither module is imported from the
   150	`MIPStarRE.QPBT` umbrella — that keeps the audits out of ordinary downstream
   151	imports — so a plain `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT` does not run them and they have
   152	to be named, as above.
   153	
   154	To read the closures directly instead, put this in a scratch file at the root of
   155	the unpacked snapshot and elaborate it with `lake env lean scratch.lean`:
   156	
   157	```lean
   158	import MIPStarRE.QPBT
   159	
   160	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness
   161	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit
   162	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one
   163	#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness
   164	```
   165

  1694		% conjugation estimates of lem:qld-unitary, which concern the
  1695		% unitarily conjugated operators V (M_h ot Id) V^dagger, to the
  1696		% corresponding estimates for the isometry phi, whose conjugation
  1697		% inserts the projection onto its range; the range-projection
  1698		% argument below supplies the missing step.
  1699		Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} concerns the unitarily conjugated operators $N^W_h = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$, whereas conjugation by the isometry $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ additionally inserts the projection $Q_{\mathrm{A}} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ onto the range of $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$: since $(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}$ act on disjoint registers and hence commute,

  1704		\]

  1711		\]

  1713		\[

  1725		The formal game uses one answer alphabet for all question types.  Its
  1726		internal Pauli-family construction therefore completes the prescribed
  1727		answers by folding every malformed answer into outcome zero.  For either
  1728		player the completed zero effect is the raw zero effect plus the malformed
  1729		answer effect, while all nonzero effects agree.  Rejection on the two
  1730		oriented Pauli--point edges bounds the malformed mass by a universal
  1731		multiple of $\eps$.  Contractivity and the state estimate then bound its
  1732		action on the ideal state by a universal multiple of
  1733		$\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}^2+\eps$.  The squared triangle inequality transfers
  1734		the completed estimates to the raw effects printed in
  1735		Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}; enlarging the existential prefactor $a$ absorbs
  1736		this loss without changing the displayed form or exponent.  This

  1743	\begin{remark}[Norm conventions in the robustness bound]\label{rem:pauli-robustness-form}
  1744		The proof above, following the source, establishes the first conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in the squared form $\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, whereas the theorem bounds the unsquared norm by $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$.   1747	\section{Formalization support for the robustness bound}

  1750	article.  It records, as a single inequality, the adjustment of the universal
  1751	constants of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} that is used when the robustness bound is
  1752	passed from its squared to its unsquared form, and when several estimates are
  1753	brought to a common scale.

  1755	\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of the robustness bound in its universal constants]\label{lem:delta-qld-mono-support}
  1756		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaQld_mono}
  1757		\leanok
  1758		\uses{thm:pauli}
  1759		Write $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}^{a,b}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a\bigl(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}\bigr)$ for the soundness function of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} with universal constants $a$ and $b$. Let $(q,m,d)$ be an admissible parameter tuple (Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), let $1 \le a \le a'$, let $0 < b' \le b$, and let $0 \le \eps \le 1$. Then
  1760		\[
  1761			\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}^{a,b}(\eps,m,d,q) \le \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}^{a',b'}(\eps,m,d,q)\;.
  1762		\]
  1763	\end{lemma}
  1764	\begin{proof}
  1765		\leanok
  1766		\uses{def:admissible}
  1767		Admissibility gives $md \ge 1$ and $q \ge 1$, so $a(md)^a \le a'(md)^{a'}$. In the bracket, $\eps^b \le \eps^{b'}$ because $0 \le \eps \le 1$ and $0 < b' \le b$; $q^{-b} \le q^{-b'}$ because $q \ge 1$ and $-b \le -b'$; and $2^{-bmd} \le 2^{-b'md}$ because $md \ge 0$ and $-bmd \le -b'md$.   1768	\end{proof}

     2	
     3	This directory generates the self-contained statement files used by the
     4	companion challenge repositories to verify, with the official
     5	[leanprover/comparator](https://github.com/leanprover/comparator), that this
     6	library proves the headline theorems.  Background and trust model:
     7	`docs/comparator.md`.
     8	
     9	Two challenges are configured today, one entry each in `challenges.py`:
    10	
    11	| Challenge | Target theorems | Generated file | Challenge repository |
    12	|---|---|---|---|
    13	| `ldt` | `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` | `expected/Challenge.lean.expected` | [LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator) |
    14	| `qpbt` | `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`, `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` | `expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected` | [QPBT-comparator](https://github.com/Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator) |
    15	
    16	Each generated file imports only Mathlib and re-declares, verbatim and in
    17	dependency order, every declaration in the kernel closure of the target
    18	statements, each with a provenance comment; the target theorems themselves are
    19	stated with `sorry`.
    20	
    21	## Adding or changing a challenge
    22	
    23	`challenges.py` is the single source of truth: one `Challenge` entry carries
    24	the target theorem names, the header and footer that frame the generated file,
    25	the path of the checked-in expected copy, and the two elaboration-context
    26	tables described under *Maintenance notes*.  A new challenge therefore needs an
    27	entry, a header, a footer, and one CI drift step — no generator code changes.
    28	
    29	The extractor is shared.  It imports the root module of every configured
    30	challenge and reads its roots from the `COMPARATOR_TARGETS` environment
    31	variable (whitespace-separated, defaulting to the LDT root), so a new challenge
    32	whose targets live outside the current imports also needs its root module added
    33	to `extract_closure.lean`.
    34	
    35	## Drift guard and regeneration
    36	
    37	The repository keeps each generated challenge checked in under
    38	`scripts/comparator/expected/`.  The final `.expected` suffix keeps these
    39	generated, intentionally monolithic fixtures out of the 1000-line
    40	project-source guard.  The PR CI guard regenerates each challenge in a
    41	temporary directory and byte-compares it with the checked-in copy; it never
    42	writes a challenge file at the repository root.
    43	
    44	Run the deterministic guard from the repository root (requires a built
    45	library).  With no `--challenge` every configured challenge is checked:
    46	
    47	```sh
    48	python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root .
    49	python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --challenge qpbt
    50	```
    51	
    52	To update the checked-in expected copies after an intentional statement or
    53	dependency change, run the exact maintenance command:
    54	
    55	```sh
    56	python3 scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py --root . --update
    57	```
    58	
    59	or, for one challenge only, add `--challenge ldt` / `--challenge qpbt`.
    60	
    61	The update command performs the documented extraction and assembly pipeline in a
    62	temporary directory (shown here for the QPBT challenge):
    63	
    64	```sh
    65	# 1. extract the closure of the statements of the challenge's targets
    66	#    (a Lean metaprogram mirroring comparator's runForUsedConsts traversal)
    67	COMPARATOR_TARGETS="MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit" \
    68	  lake env lean scripts/comparator/extract_closure.lean > closure.tsv
    69	awk -F'\t' 'NF==4' closure.tsv > closure.clean.tsv
    70	
    71	# 2. assemble the challenge file (topological order, namespace handling)
    72	python3 scripts/comparator/assemble_challenge.py closure.clean.tsv \
    73	    --challenge qpbt > draft.lean
    74	cat scripts/comparator/challenge_qpbt_header.lean draft.lean \
    75	    scripts/comparator/challenge_qpbt_footer.lean \
    76	    > scripts/comparator/expected/ChallengeQPBT.lean.expected
    77	```
    78	
    79	Then copy the expected file into the challenge repository as `Challenge.lean`,
    80	bump the `rev` pin in its `lakefile.toml` to the library commit it was
    81	generated from, and run its `./verify.sh` (its CI also runs on every push).
    82	
    83	## Maintenance notes
    84	
    85	- A challenge's `extras`/`module_preludes` tables carry elaboration context
    86	  (attribute commands, `CoeFun` instances, `variable`/`open` blocks) that the
    87	  kernel closure cannot see.  Extend them if regeneration produces compile
    88	  errors in the generated file; the script fails loudly if a table key no
    89	  longer matches any extracted declaration.
    90	- The target statements in each footer mirror the theorems in the library:
    91	  `challenge_footer.lean` mirrors
    92	  `MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/MainTheorem/MainFormal.lean`, and
    93	  `challenge_qpbt_footer.lean` mirrors `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean`

    98	  and `autoParam` helpers) are emitted as explanatory comments; they

   102	  library's name.  Closure members found to be private are made public in the

   127	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   128	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%

   132	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   133	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization

   137	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   138	There, the combined point measurements
   139	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   140	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   141	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   142	individual degree game with parameters
   143	\[
   144	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   145	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   146	\]
   147	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   148	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   149	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   150	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   151	
   152	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   153	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   154	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   155	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   156	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   157	$\chi(s)$ with
   158	\[
   159	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   160	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   161	\]
   162	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   163	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   164	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.

   166	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   167	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   168	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   169	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   170	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   171	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   172	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   173	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility.  Thus even before the
   174	two soundness-import obligations below are considered, this route can apply to

   178	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   179	
   180	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   181	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   182	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   183	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   184	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   185	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   187	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   188	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   189	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   190	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   191	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   192	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   193	open for the printed tensor-code route. Both obligations are independent of
   194	the divisibility question and remain open for that route at every dimension
   195	where that game is defined.  They would also arise from an attempt to prove
   196	soundness of the directly indexed game by the same tensor-code import.  The
   197	established proof for the directly indexed game takes a different route through
   198	the low individual degree theorem and therefore bypasses both obligations.
   199	
   200	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   201	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   202	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   203	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   204	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   205	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   206	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   207	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   208	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   209	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   210	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   211	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   212	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   213	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   214	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   215	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   216	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   217	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   218	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   219	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   220	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   221	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   222	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   223	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   224	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   225	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   226	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   227	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   228	
   229	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   230	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   231	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   232	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   233	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   234	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   235	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   236	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   237	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   238	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   239	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   240	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   241	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   242	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   243	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   244	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   245	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   246	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   247	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's carry
   248	only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   249	$\chi^{-1}(i)$.  For the comparison with the directly indexed game, this

   251	averaged away, as explained below.  That construction resolves this part of

   253	pair-question construction required for the tensor-code test.

    40	\section{Key theorem forms}
    41	
    42	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    43	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    44	\[
    45	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    46	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    47	\]
    48	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    49	\[
    50	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    51	  \qquad
    52	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    53	\]
    54	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    55	\[
    56	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    57	\]
    58	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    59	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    60	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    61	
    62	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    63	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    64	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    65	\[
    66	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    67	\]
    68	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    69	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    70	$\Delta$.

    95	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    96	
    97	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    98	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    99	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
   100	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
   101	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   102	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   103	
   104	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   105	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   106	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   107	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   108	\[
   109	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   110	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   111	\]
   112	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   113	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   114	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   115	
   116	The finite-dimensional estimate is proved in
   117	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/RangeProjection.lean}. For a complete POVM
   118	$\{N_h\}$, an orthogonal projection $Q$, and $Q\vartheta=\vartheta$, it gives
   119	\[
   120	  \sum_h\|(N_hQ-T_h)\Delta\|^2
   121	  \le 2\sum_h\|(N_h-T_h)\Delta\|^2+2\|\Delta-\vartheta\|^2.
   122	\]
   123	The proof uses $\sum_h N_h^\dagger N_h\le I$, so it also applies when the
   124	measurement is not projective. The same module proves the isometry form under
   125	the exact identity $N_h\phi=\phi M_h$ and its two bipartite placements. The
   126	unit-ancilla embedding and its composition with a unitary, including the
   127	identity $U(M\ot I\ot I)U^\dagger\phi=\phi M$, are proved in
   128	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/Ancilla.lean} for $\phi=UJ$,
   129	$J\psi=\psi\ot\eta$, $\|\eta\|=1$, and $U^\dagger U=I$.
   130	
   131	The supplied-data transfer is proved in
   132	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/StateTransfer.lean} and
   133	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/OperatorTransfer.lean}. Given an actual
   134	\path{ExtractionWitness}, the local maps adjoin a normalized EPR state and
   135	apply its swap unitaries. Register reassociation identifies their tensor
   136	action with the witness's transformed state, so its squared distance from
   137	the ideal state is at most $\delta$. The existing swapped total-Pauli POVMs
   138	intertwine with these maps; the two bipartite range-projection estimates
   139	bound each full squared operator-family sum by $4\delta$. Thus the same
   140	\path{PauliSoundnessWitness} satisfies all three soundness estimates at
   141	$\max\{\sqrt\delta,4\delta\}$. This is an auxiliary result with supplied
   142	extraction data, not a new bridge field or a proof of soundness for arbitrary
   143	strategies.

    68	\section{Key theorem forms}
    69	
    70	Throughout, $(q,m,d)$ is an admissible parameter tuple of the Pauli basis
    71	test, $\ket{\hat\psi}$ is the expanded state of the projective strategy
    72	under analysis, succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, and all
    73	approximations are with respect to $\ket{\hat\psi}$.  For lines
    74	$\ell_X, \ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$, the POVM $\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$,
    75	with outcomes pairs of polynomials of degree at most $md$ on the two
    76	lines, is the two-basis combined line measurement, and
    77	$\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ is the combined point measurement; their
    78	consistency errors are $\delta_P = \poly(\eps, md/q)$ and
    79	$\delta_Q = \poly(\eps)$ respectively, and
    80	$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}} = \poly(\eps)$ is the line--point consistency
    81	error of the strategy.  The lemma under discussion asserts that a
    82	measurement $\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, built for each line $\ell$ in
    83	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, is $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$-consistent, on average over
    84	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$, with the combined point
    85	measurement on the extended coordinates, together with the
    86	register-swapped counterpart.%
    87	\footnote{In the mirror of the source consulted here,
    88	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}: the
    89	lemma statement, with the error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, is at
    90	lines~1020--1034 (label \path{lem:qld-4-13}); the central display with
    91	the first-route bound at lines~1134--1137
    92	(label \path{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}); the three claims at
    93	lines~1140--1239 (labels \path{claim:17-1}--\path{claim:17-3}); the
    94	second-route conclusion $O(m^2\delta_P)$ at lines~1241--1245, preceded by
    95	a duplicated sentence whose second copy carries a malformed reference;
    96	the product-distribution estimate invoked there at lines~1055--1061
    97	(label \path{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}); and the sub-line lemma at
    98	lines~1063--1116 (label \path{lem:qld-sublines}).}
    99	The comparison involves four forms of the error function
   100	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}(\eps,m,d,q)$.
   101	\begin{enumerate}
   102	  \item \textbf{Source form.}
   103	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = \poly(m^2\eps,\, md/q)$.  This is the form
   104	  printed in the statement.  Neither printed derivation supports it.
   105	  \item \textbf{Established form (first route).}
   106	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}
   107	  = O\big(m\,(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4}
   108	  + \delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2})\big)$, a function of the form
   109	  $m \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$.
   110	  \item \textbf{Second-route form (conditional).}
   111	  $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = O(m^2 \delta_P)
   112	  = m^2 \cdot \poly(\eps,\, md/q)$, conditional on a joint-law
   113	  decomposition that the sub-line lemma, as stated, does not provide.
   114	  \item \textbf{Consumer requirement.}  The unique consumer, the
   115	  polynomial-pair lemma, feeds $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$ into an error
   116	  of the form
   117	  $a(md)^a(\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ imported
   118	  from \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}; any bound
   119	  $m^{O(1)} \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ is absorbed by enlarging $a$ and
   120	  shrinking $b$, so forms~2 and~3 both suffice downstream.
   121	\end{enumerate}

   123	\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}
   124	
   125	The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
   126	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   127	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   128	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   129	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   130	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   131	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   132	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   133	
   134	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   135	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   136	order
   137	\[
   138	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   139	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   140	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   141	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   142	\]
   143	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   144	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   145	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   146	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   147	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   148	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   149	
   150	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   151	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   152	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   153	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   154	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   155	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   156	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   157	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   158	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   159	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
   160	mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
   161	$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
   162	law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
   163	$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
   164	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
   165	counterexample theorem is asserted here.
   166	
   167	The repaired conditional helper has the form
   168	\[
   169	  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   170	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   171	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   172	  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   173	\]
   174	This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
   175	declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
   176	it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
   177	point construction, then applies the conditional helper.
   178	
   179	The construction theorem is
   180	\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
   181	with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it proves evaluated consistency
   182	of the explicit unconditioned measurement
   183	\[
   184	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   185	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   186	\]
   187	under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
   188	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite
   189	placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
   190	pasting argument at lines 942--961 supply the proof. The POVM,
   191	axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.
   192	
   193	The proof conditions the sampling law on the event that the X direction
   194	is nonzero, whose probability lies between $1/2$ and $1$. It leaves the
   195	measurement unchanged. On this event, the polynomial root bound gives the
   196	conditional collision estimate needed for pasting. Multiplication by the
   197	retained probability and addition of the discarded contribution, at most
   198	$1/(2q)$, restore the original product law. Thus the result concerns the
   199	unconditioned X-Z-X measurement, with no conditioning premise in its
   200	statement. The current heterogeneous pasting theorem requires only the two
   201	forward marginal comparisons, both supplied by the point-to-line estimates.
   202	
   203	The directly indexed auxiliary
   204	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established} then constructs the point
   205	witness internally, conditions the subline law on each extended line, and
   206	averages the polynomial combination of these actual paired-line effects.
   207	The real-part overlap estimates for both opposite placements give the
   208	corrected bound $C m\,\poly(\eps,md/q)$. This construction retains the
   209	completed answer alphabet and the directly indexed question law; it does not
   210	discharge their comparison with the printed source theorem.\footnote{The
   211	proof and its necessary dependencies were selectively recovered for
   212	\ghissue{512} from commit
   213	\path{6e8d67ef8ba22de69a0c166adcdf23ba6e7a33aa}, retained at
   214	\path{0f4ef05370350f4017439ebd839ef0561f13130f}. See
   215	\path{audits/2026-09-12_issue512-saved-proof-recovery.md} for the
   216	signature audit, axiom closure, and cumulative cost accounting.}

   218	\subsection{The extended-line supplied-point obstruction}

   260	The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly

   262	of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.

     1	# MIPStarRE — the quantum Pauli basis test, formalized in Lean 4
     2	
     3	This repository contains a machine-checked formalization of the **quantum
     4	Pauli basis test** of *MIP\* = RE* ([arXiv:2001.04383](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04383)),
     5	together with the classical **low individual degree test** it is built on
     6	(*Quantum soundness of the classical low individual degree test*,
     7	[arXiv:2009.12982](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.12982)). The source sections are
     8	mirrored in-repo under `references/`; the Pauli basis test is developed in
     9	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex`.
    10	
    11	| | |
    12	|---|---|
    13	| Headline theorem | `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`, `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean:52` |
    14	| Proof debt | none — **0 `sorry`**, 0 `admit`, 0 project `axiom` declarations |
    15	| Axioms used | `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only |
    16	| Toolchain | Lean `v4.32.0`, Mathlib `v4.32.0` (rev `81a5d257c8e4`), pinned in `lean-toolchain` and `lake-manifest.json` |
    17	| Size | Pauli development 330 Lean files / 105,319 lines; `MIPStarRE/LDT/` 326 files; `MIPStarRE/Quantum/` 11 files |
    18	
    19	## What is formalized
    20	
    21	The Pauli basis test is a two-player nonlocal game whose soundness is one of the
    22	rigidity ingredients of *MIP\* = RE*. The headline results:
    23	
    24	| Result | Lean declaration | File |
    25	|---|---|---|
    26	| Soundness of the Pauli basis test (blueprint `thm:pauli`) | `pauli_soundness` | `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean:52` |
    27	| Qubit form of soundness (`cor:pauli-binary`) | `pauli_soundness_qubit` | `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/QubitForm.lean:423` |
    28	| Completeness: a value-one strategy exists (`lem:pauli-completeness`) | `exists_spcc_value_one` | `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Completeness.lean:266` |
    29	| Quantum soundness of the low-degree game (`lem:ld-soundness`) | `exists_ld_soundness` | `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean:82` |
    30	
    31	`pauli_soundness` states: there are constants `a ≥ 1` and `0 < b < 1` such that
    32	for every admissible parameter tuple `P` and every `ε ≥ 0`, every strategy for
    33	the Pauli basis test with value at least `1 - ε` admits local isometries and an
    34	auxiliary state under which the strategy's state is within
    35	`deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q` of the ideal state, and both players' operator
    36	families are within the same bound of the ideal Pauli observables. The error
    37	scale carries the admissible sizes as explicit arguments —
    38	`deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ)`, `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/SoundnessDefs.lean:35` —
    39	because it is `a · (m·d)^a · (ε^b + q^(-b) + 2^(-b·m·d))`: the bound depends on
    40	the admissible sizes `m`, `d` and `q` as well as on `ε`, which is what the
    41	`q^(-b)` and `2^(-b·m·d)` terms express. As in the source, the constants are
    42	existentially quantified and no regime in which `deltaQld < 1` is exhibited;
    43	see [`docs/DEVIATIONS.md`](docs/DEVIATIONS.md).
    44	
    45	Every headline declaration carries a docstring naming both its blueprint node
    46	and the exact source line range it formalizes, for example
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`
    48	for `pauli_soundness`.
    49	
    50	The classical low individual degree test underneath is
    51	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal`; the Pauli development imports it and does not
    52	re-derive it.
    53	
    54	## Status
    55	
    56	- **No proof debt.** There is no `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide`, `unsafe`
    57	  declaration or project-introduced `axiom` anywhere in the Lean sources under
    58	  `MIPStarRE/`. In the `.lean` files of the whole tree the word `sorry` occurs
    59	  exactly four times: twice in prose inside docstrings
    60	  (`MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean:81`,
    61	  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Apply.lean:57`), once in prose in
    62	  `scripts/comparator/challenge_header.lean:14`, and once as real syntax in
    63	  `scripts/comparator/challenge_footer.lean:44` — the footer of a
    64	  statement-only challenge template that is supposed to be unproved (see
    65	  "Independent checking" below). One further file is Lean-shaped without
    66	  carrying the `.lean` extension: `scripts/comparator/expected/Challenge.lean.expected`,
    67	  the checked-in expected assembly of that same template, repeats the prose
    68	  mention (line 14) and the template's `sorry` (line 802);
    69	  `scripts/comparator/README.md:14` mentions it in prose as well. These counts
    70	  are about source files: the string also
    71	  occurs throughout the development records under `results/telemetry/` and in
    72	  the documentation, so a bare `git grep sorry` over the whole tree returns
    73	  thousands of lines.
    74	- **Standard axioms only.** The headline theorems depend on `propext`,
    75	  `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` and on nothing else. There is no
    76	  dedicated Pauli-test axiom-audit module yet — the existing
    77	  [`MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean`](MIPStarRE/LDT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean)
    78	  covers the classical low-degree track only — so the check is made by asking
    79	  Lean directly; the command is under "Build and check" below. Repository-wide,
    80	  the pre-push gate (`.githooks/pre-push`) runs
    81	  [`scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py`](scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py)
    82	  `--ci`, which runs `#print axioms` on every blueprint declaration marked
    83	  `\leanok` and fails if any of them depends on `sorryAx`.
    84	- **Statement corrections are documented, not hidden.** Where the source
    85	  paper's printed statement is wrong, or where its printed proof does not
    86	  establish the printed claim, the deviation is recorded rather than papered
    87	  over. There are 20 Pauli-test gap notes (45 notes in total; the directory
    88	  also holds `command.tex`, `template.tex`, `policy.tex` and
    89	  `proof-gap-protocol.tex`, which are not notes) under
    90	  `docs/paper-gaps/`, summarized in the register linked below. Two printed
    91	  claims that are not established are carried as `Prop`-valued definitions
    92	  which state the source sentence without asserting it, so the printed form
    93	  stays visible and stays unproved.
    94	- **Independent checking.** There is no comparator challenge for
    95	  `pauli_soundness` yet. What can be re-checked outside this repository today
    96	  is the classical low individual degree test underneath: the statement
    97	  `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` has a challenge repository at
    98	  [LionSR/LDT-comparator](https://github.com/LionSR/LDT-comparator), which
    99	  re-declares the statement against Mathlib alone and runs the Lean comparator
   100	  against this library; the setup is described in
   101	  [`docs/comparator.md`](docs/comparator.md), and the template it is assembled
   102	  from lives under `scripts/comparator/`. The analogous challenge for the
   103	  Pauli statement has not been built: `Dengnifer/QPBT-comparator` is so far a
   104	  placeholder holding only a licence and a toolchain pin.
   105	
   106	## Build and check
   107	
   108	Install [elan](https://github.com/leanprover/elan); it reads `lean-toolchain`
   109	and fetches Lean `v4.32.0` automatically. From the repository root:
   110	
   111	```bash
   112	lake exe cache get              # fetch the pinned Mathlib build cache (required)
   113	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT       # build the Pauli basis test development
   114	lake build MIPStarRE            # build everything (QPBT, LDT, Quantum)
   115	```
   116	
   117	To reproduce the axiom claim, ask Lean for the axiom closure of a headline
   118	declaration:
   119	
   120	```bash
   121	lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.Soundness
   122	printf 'import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.Soundness\n#print axioms MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness\n' > AxiomCheck.lean
   123	lake env lean AxiomCheck.lean
   124	```
   125	
   126	`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` are the only axioms that should
   127	appear; in particular `sorryAx` must not. The same recipe applies to the other
   128	three headline declarations, with their own modules imported.
   129	
   130	To type-check a single file, which is the fastest iteration loop:
   131	
   132	```bash
   133	lake env lean MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean
   134	```
   135	
   136	### Build time and machine requirements
   137	
   138	Timings below are the recorded ones from `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`
   139	(1,608 rows), all measured on one machine: a 128-core Intel Xeon Platinum 8358P
   140	at 2.60 GHz with 503 GiB of RAM.

   142	| Kind of build | Rows | Median | Range |
   143	|---|---|---|---|
   144	| Incremental build of touched modules | 1,248 | 37 s | 17 s – 4,428 s |
   145	| Fresh worktree seeded from a warm local cache | 172 | 75 s | 5 s – 25,052 s |
   146	
   147	Recent fresh-worktree builds of the full tree took 219 s, 227 s, 229 s and
   148	502 s. The 25,052 s (≈ 7 h) outlier is a single from-scratch run of
   149	2026-08-30 that also compiled 20 Mathlib files the cache failed to deliver;
   150	it predates most of the Pauli development and is not a measurement of the
   151	current tree.
   152	
   153	**A clean-clone build of `MIPStarRE.QPBT` has not yet been timed and recorded.**
   154	All rows above were produced with a warm local build cache, so they are lower
   155	bounds on what a fresh clone costs. Budget accordingly, and expect the
   156	`lake exe cache get` download of Mathlib to dominate the first build. 23 files
   157	raise `maxHeartbeats` and 17 raise `synthInstance.maxSize`; these are
   158	elaboration-budget options, not soundness escapes.
   159	
   160	The blueprint is built with [`leanblueprint`](https://github.com/PatrickMassot/leanblueprint):
   161	
   162	```bash
   163	leanblueprint pdf     # PDF output
   164	leanblueprint web     # HTML output
   165	```
   166	
   167	`leanblueprint` also generates `blueprint/lean_decls`, the list of declarations
   168	the blueprint cross-references; `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`
   169	verifies that each one exists.
   170

   172	
   173	```

   175	├── QPBT/          # Quantum Pauli basis test — the contribution

   309	\section{Repairs and current status}
   310	
   311	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (soundness established).}
   312	For arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the formalization defines the line-point
   313	distribution over $\F_q^{m'}$ by sampling the point, the axis index
   314	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   315	$i-1$ coordinates directly.  In the resulting game, line questions carry
   316	the index $i$ (and, for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place
   317	of the seed $s \in \F_q$.  Soundness form~4 is established for this game
   318	through the low individual degree theorem and the general-simultaneity
   319	combining reduction analysed in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich}.
   320	This removes the divisibility obstruction for the
   321	auxiliary directly indexed game.  Because the proof does not use the
   322	tensor-code import, it leaves both original import obligations open rather
   323	than establishing them.
   324	
   325	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must be proved at the level
   326	of strategies, not merely of question distributions.  An
   327	$\mathsf{ALine}$ question of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0,s)$ and a
   328	$\mathsf{DLine}$ question is a triple $(u_0,s,v')$, so measurements may vary
   329	between seeds in the same class $\chi^{-1}(i)$.  Each seed nevertheless has a
   330	unique decomposition into its index $i$ and a residue
   331	$\rho\in\{0,\ldots,q/m'-1\}$.  The seed-indexed question law is thereby
   332	identified with the direct question law together with a uniform residue; the
   333	parsing map back to the direct question law is an exact pushforward.
   334	
   335	The formal transport retains, rather than averages away, the dependence on
   336	$\rho$.  It adjoins a register of dimension $q/m'$ to each player's Hilbert
   337	space, places the two registers in a maximally correlated state, and makes
   338	each question measurement block diagonal, with the block at $\rho$ equal to
   339	the original measurement for the corresponding seed.  Thus both players see
   340	the same residue on a synchronicity branch.  This correlated-residue lift
   341	preserves normalization and projectivity and preserves the game value exactly,
   342	branch by branch.  In particular, seed-dependent relabellings cause no loss;
   343	the earlier obstruction arose only from independently averaging the local
   344	measurements, which is not the construction used here.%
   345	\footnote{The exact distribution comparison is formalized in
   346	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Correspondence.lean}.
   347	The lift, projectivity theorem, and value identity are
   348	\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect},
   349	\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect\_isProjective}, and
   350	\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect\_value\_eq} in
   351	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/SeedFiber.lean} and
   352	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/SeedFiberValue.lean}.}
   353	
   354	Applying form~4 to the lifted strategy produces polynomial-tuple POVMs
   355	$G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$ on the enlarged carriers.  Compress one
   356	such POVM by taking the normalized average of its diagonal residue blocks.
   357	When the other family is a point measurement, it is constant on the opposite
   358	residue register, and this compression preserves the associated defect
   359	exactly.  Consequently the point/polynomial and polynomial/point conclusions
   360	of the directly indexed theorem transport back to the original seed-indexed
   361	strategy with no additional error.%
   362	\footnote{These two identities are
   363	\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect\_pointPolynomial\_compression} and
   364	\leanid{ldStrategyToDirect\_polynomialPoint\_compression} in
   365	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Consistency/Compression.lean}.}
   366	
   367	The third conclusion is different.  On the lifted state, the
   368	global/global defect pairs equal residues.  Compressing both polynomial
   369	measurements separately instead produces a double average over independent
   370	residues.  Neither quantity bounds the other in general.  For example, on a
   371	two-element residue register, if both deterministic measurements report the
   372	residue, the equal-residue disagreement is zero while the independent-residue
   373	disagreement is $1/2$.  If Alice reports the residue and Bob reports its
   374	complement, the corresponding disagreements are $1$ and $1/2$. For every $k$,
   375	the third relation is instead recovered on the original Hilbert spaces.
   376	The point-agreement branch has weight $1/9$, so the two point measurements
   377	have consistency defect at most $9\eps$. The triangle inequality combines
   378	this with the two compressed mixed relations to give agreement of evaluated
   379	polynomial tuples. Distinct tuples differ in at least one coordinate, so
   380	their evaluations can agree only where those two coordinate polynomials
   381	agree. Schwartz--Zippel therefore gives the same collision bound $m'd/q$
   382	for every $k$, without a union bound over the coordinates.
   383	Writing $E=\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,k)$ for the direct error, the
   384	global defect after compression is at most
   385	\[
   386	  E+2\sqrt{9\eps+E}+\frac{m'd}{q}.
   387	\]
   388	For $\eps\leq1$ the direct error dominates both $\eps$ and $m'd/q$.
   389	If also $E\leq1$, the displayed expression is at most $10\sqrt E$.
   390	Replacing the direct constants $(a,b)$ by $(10a,b/2)$ absorbs this bound:
   391	the square root of a sum is at most the sum of its square roots, and the
   392	prefactor $a(dm'k)^a$ is at least one. When $E>1$ or $\eps>1$, the unit
   393	bound on bipartite consistency defects suffices. This proves seed-indexed
   394	soundness for every $k$.%
   395	\footnote{The point-agreement estimates are proved in
   396	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/PointAgreement.lean}.
   397	The resulting theorem is \leanid{exists\_ld\_soundness} in
   398	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/LowDegreeGameTheorems.lean}; the scalar estimate is
   399	\leanid{ten\_sqrt\_deltaLd\_le} in
   400	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/SeedError.lean}.}
   401	
   402	The combining reduction has now been formalized with the direct distribution
   403	and the directly indexed game, so it is well defined at dimension
   404	$m'+\kappa$ for
   405	all positive parameters.  Its proof uses the sampled geometric data and then
   406	applies the low individual degree theorem at the combined dimension.  This
   407	establishes soundness of the directly indexed game and, by the compression
   408	and recovery argument above, of the seed-indexed game. The directly indexed
   409	application at dimension $2m+2$ now also constructs the global polynomial-pair
   410	measurement, as \leanid{exists\_globalPairWitness} in
   411	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Apply.lean}. This proves the polynomial-pair
   412	conclusion without a divisibility hypothesis. It does not identify the
   413	undefined source seed law with the direct law or prove the intervening
   414	source-shaped subline statements.
   415	The external check that the tensor-code test of arXiv:2111.08131 samples
   416	its axes and subcubes directly has been made against that source: Figure~1
   417	there draws the axis index and the subcube data uniformly and directly,
   418	with no index encoding into $\F_q$.
   419	
   420	\paragraph{Padding the dimension.}
   421	Alternatively, embed the combined polynomial into
   422	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,\bar m}(\F_q)$ for $\bar m = 4m$, the least power of two
   423	with $\bar m \ge 2m+2$, ignoring the $2m-2$ dummy variables.  Then
   424	$\bar m \mid q$ holds whenever $q \ge 4m$, and the existing game applies at
   425	dimension $\bar m$.  In the complementary regime $m \in \{q/2,\, q\}$ the
   426	conclusion is vacuous: $md \ge q/2$ gives
   427	$\delta_S \ge a(md)^a q^{-b} \ge a\,2^{-a} q^{a-b} \ge a\,2^{-b} \ge 1$
   428	for $a \ge 2$, while the consistency quantities bounded by the theorem never
   429	exceed $1$.  This route stays inside the present definitions but reworks the
   430	sub-line distribution (a fourth coordinate block of dummies), the combining
   431	map, and the wrong-block Schwartz--Zippel analysis, and it moves the
   432	combining lemmas away from their source statements at dimension $2m+2$.
   433	
   434	\paragraph{Unequal index classes.}
   435	One could instead define an index function at dimension $2m+2$ with classes
   436	of sizes $\lfloor q/(2m+2)\rfloor$ and $\lceil q/(2m+2)\rceil$.  The index
   437	is then only approximately uniform, the identification with the external
   438	test fails exactly, and every distributional identity in the sub-line
   439	analysis acquires an error term; this amounts to re-proving the imported
   440	soundness theorem for a perturbed game and is not recommended.

   543	\section{Comparison with the blueprint}
   544	
   545	The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} keeps the sub-line lemma, the
   546	combined line lemma, and the polynomial-pair lemma in their source-shaped
   547	statements, with no divisibility hypothesis.  Their proofs retain the source
   548	constructions and mark the unresolved obligation at the exact steps: the
   549	first sampling step of the sub-line construction, where $\chi_{2m+2}$ and
   550	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ are invoked, and the
   551	instantiation step of the polynomial-pair proof, where $(q,2m+2,d,1)$ is
   552	used as a game parameter tuple.  A chapter remark records the divisibility
   553	arithmetic and cites this note. The global polynomial-pair conclusion and
   554	the final Pauli soundness theorem now have complete proofs through the
   555	directly indexed construction; the source-law assertions described here
   556	remain distinct obligations. The blueprint's proof node
   557	for the classical soundness import itself states the source's route --- the
   558	identification with the two-prover tensor-code test and the application of
   559	Theorem~4.7 --- and enumerates the two obligations of
   560	Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations} as open, citing this note for the
   561	detailed comparison and the case arithmetic.  The separate support node for
   562	general simultaneity records the established directly indexed theorem and its
   563	proof through the low individual degree theorem. The seed-indexed theorem
   564	is now proved by compression and global recovery for arbitrary $k$.
   565	A further support node, placed directly after the paper-labelled soundness
   566	theorem, records that formalized route, so that the proof-level formalization
   567	mark sits on the route the Lean proof takes rather than on the printed one;
   568	the two obligations of Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations} stay open on the
   569	paper-labelled node.
   570	An earlier revision had
   571	instead added the hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$ to the three lemmas; that was
   572	statement drift in the sense of the proof-gap protocol, since the hypothesis
   573	excludes all admissible $m \ge 2$ and does not appear in the source.
   574	
   575	\section{Conclusion}
   576	
   577	There remains a theorem-level gap in the source proof route.  The classical
   578	low individual degree game invoked at dimension $2m+2$ is undefined for every
   579	admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ (and for $(q,m)=(2,1)$), because its question
   580	distribution requires $2m+2 \mid q$ while admissibility supplies only
   581	$m \mid q$.  Independently, the source import still requires a reduction to
   582	the two-prover tensor-code test with a value bound and a valid choice of
   583	$K \ge 12m'(d+1)$; the printed choice $K=(m')^3d$ fails at the small
   584	dimensions listed in Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}.
   585	
   586	Soundness of the directly indexed game is now established at arbitrary
   587	dimension by a different proof through the low individual degree theorem and
   588	the general-simultaneity combining reduction.  That proof checks the separate
   589	condition $400Md \le N$ for $M=m'+\kappa$ and $N=2560000M^3d$.  It neither
   590	applies the tensor-code theorem nor verifies its bound on $K$, so it bypasses
   591	rather than discharges both source-import obligations.  The correlated-residue
   592	lift now transports projectivity, game value, and the two mixed consistency
   593	conclusions from this direct proof. For every $k$, point agreement and
   594	Schwartz--Zippel recover the global relation on the original Hilbert spaces,
   595	completing the seed-indexed soundness theorem without asserting a false
   596	double-compression identity.
   597	The global polynomial-pair conclusion is also proved by the directly indexed
   598	construction. What remains is the source-law correspondence of the intermediate
   599	subline assertions, not another proof of that conclusion. Repairing the
   600	original tensor-code import would provide another route to soundness, subject
   601	to the source instantiation obstruction above.

   262	\section{Conclusion}
   263	
   264	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   265	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   266	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   267	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   268	the latter has a proved general estimate and an application to the concrete
   269	extraction data. The global polynomial-pair witness
   270	and the three pulled-apart consistency estimates are now composed in a proved
   271	source-facing theorem, including at zero error. The conditional extraction
   272	theorem remains useful for a supplied global measurement, and its composition
   273	with the proved global constructor establishes the source-facing existence
   274	claim of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} for projective strategies. Its concrete
   275	isometry transfer, including the state and both operator estimates, is proved
   276	for supplied extraction data. Composing that transfer with the internally
   277	constructed data proves the restricted projective-setting isometry bounds.
   278	The Naimark reduction then removes the projectivity restriction with exact
   279	value preservation, the operator-family transfer returns both Pauli families
   280	to the original spaces at $3\delta + 6\delta^2$, the scalar absorption returns
   281	that shape to the robustness form at prefactor $21a^2$, and monotonicity in
   282	the error parameter carries the bounds to the rest of the source error
   283	domain.  Composing these with the projective-setting bounds proves
   284	\path{pauli_soundness} on the full source domain, with axiom closure
   285	\path{propext}, \path{Classical.choice} and \path{Quot.sound};
   286	\ghissue{614} records that composition.  The seed-indexed source-game
   287	correspondence step remains open, as does the divisibility obligation of
   288	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}.
